question.text: An Investor Advisory Committee in an AIF is typically composed of:

answer.text: A majority of investor representatives, providing informed guidance to the investment manager / investment committee

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (p.158) states that an Investor Advisory Committee is not mandatory and consists of a majority of investor representatives. It provides informed guidance to the investment manager / investment committee on matters such as conflict resolution, risk management, governance, investor-manager relations and reporting, statutory or tax issues, and other investor-consideration matters. The Trap: The committee is not composed of SEBI officials, the fund's own employees, or only the custodian and auditor. Its defining feature on the source page is the majority-investor composition and its advisory (not decision-making) role. Note: Source reference: NISM Series XIX-A workbook p.158 (Investor Advisory Committee — not mandatory; majority investor representatives; informed guidance to manager/IC).
